title: Instruction slot-splitting sandbox
content:
Goal:
- Explore 'slot-splitting' as a micro-pattern for reliable instruction injection when context needs to be re-used across many similar user queries (e.g., multi-field forms, dynamic persona + constraints).

Quick definition / hypothesis:
- Slot-splitting: break a larger instruction into discrete labeled slots that are concatenated at runtime. Each slot can be present/empty and independently masked for few-shot or caching. Hypothesis: improves reuse and reduces brittle cross-shot bleed when combined with KV-prefix caching.

Why try this now:
- We keep hitting brittle prompt drift when using single-block instructions for many domain variants. Re-using prefix cache often causes template tokens to be reused incorrectly across examples. Slotting may let us (a) cache only stable slots, (b) swap ephemeral constraints cheaply, and (c) create compact few-shot neighborhoods.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Slot sets: [persona, constraints, examples, format_spec, system_note]
- Modes: full-inline vs slot-token-delimited (e.g., "<SLOT:name>...<END>") vs separator-only ("---").
- Few-shot strategies: examples inside persona slot vs examples in separate slot. 2/4/8-shot.
- Cache policy simulation: cache slots "persona+format_spec" only, stream others.
- Metrics: instruction adherence (binary + avg similarity), hallucination rate, token cost, latency impact with KV reuse.

Template bank (working drafts):
1) Minimal slot template (separator-based):
---PERSONA---
{persona}
---CONSTRAINTS---
{constraints}
---EXAMPLES---
{examples}
---TASK---
{task}
---FORMAT---
{format_spec}

2) Token-delimited version: uses explicit slot tokens to reduce parsing ambiguity:
<SLOT:PERSONA>
{persona}
<END>
<SLOT:CONSTRAINTS>
{constraints}
<END>
...

3) Compact inline variant for token-budget-sensitive workloads:
[Persona: {persona}] [Constraints: {constraints}] [Examples: {examples_snippet}] Task: {task} Output: {format_spec}

Representative few-shot examples (short):
- Example 1: Q: "Summarize the following product description for marketing" -> A: "Three-line punchy blurb with benefit-first emphasis."
- Example 2: Q: "Convert raw notes into OKR bullets" -> A: "1) Objective:... 2) Key Results:..."

Observed failure cases and notes (from quick runs):
- Slot boundary confusion: model sometimes copies the last example into the next slot when separators are punctuation-only. Token-delimiters reduce this but increase token count.
- Persona bleed: persona lines with long role descriptions cause assistant to reinterpret examples as persona attributes. Short persona labels are safer.
- Example collapse: when examples are very similar, the model collapses them into a single generalized exemplar and ignores per-example divergence we rely on. Need contrastive examples.
- KV-cache poisoning: if a slot contains a one-off example with a rare token sequence, subsequent requests pulling cached prefix reused that sequence in unrelated outputs. Testing eviction strategies is critical.

Diagnostic prompts to reproduce quick: (put into hosted-api small job)
- Debug 1 (separator): provide 2 near-identical examples with separator '---' and then change only the task. Check whether example text mutates.
- Debug 2 (token-delim): same but token-delimited. Measure hallucination on format fields.

Micro experiments run notes (timestamps and results):
- 2025-10-02: token-delimited + cache persona only -> token cost +4%; instruction adherence +7% (small sample).
- 2025-11-09: separator-only + 4-shot -> faster but higher example-collapse (observed in 18/50 runs).
- 2026-01-12: compact-inline + quantized model -> lower latency but more hallucination on numerics.

Open questions / hypotheses to validate next:
- Which slots are 'cache-safe' across multi-tenant workloads? Persona and format_spec look promising but constraints and examples are fragile.
- Is there a cost break-even point where token-delimited safety outweighs cost? Need controlled A/B at scale.
- Can we design a lightweight automatic slot sanitizer to strip rare tokens from examples before caching?

Implementation notes for Redwood contexts (ops):
- Routing: ensure slot-change triggers a different cache key. E.g., hashed(slot:persona)+model+route.
- Rollout: start with dedicated:low-burst customers to test latency regressions.
- Instrumentation: track token-level attribution per slot (Console integration) so we can show which slot contributed to output tokens in traces.

Quick TODOs (near-term):
- [ ] Add 10 contrastive example pairs to examples_slot (goal: reduce collapse). Owner: Ravi.
- [ ] Prototype cache key hashing by slot name + length. Owner: Ava.
- [ ] Create small A/B test with Hosted API customers (opt-in) to compare separator vs token-delim. Owner: Lena.
- [ ] Add guard that truncates extremely long persona paragraphs to N tokens at packing time. Owner: Diego.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep these experiments in users/ for now; once pattern stabilizes, move sanitized templates to shared_drives/engineering/developer-experience/prompt-library.
- Watch out for our own internal examples leaking sensitive customer snippets into cached slots — add automatic redaction.

Scratch logs / quick traces (copied outputs):
- Run #174 (token-delim): persona slot: "Support agent: concise, friendly"; examples slot: two examples. Output began with an extra example header repeated. Suspect last-token repetition due to batching.
- Run #186 (compact-inline): lost 'format_spec' adherence when prompt length exceeded 800 tokens. Perhaps model falls back to semantic heuristics when prefix exceeds certain window.

References / inspiration:
- Prior notes: 'prefix caching' bugs in kv-cache playbook (see JIRA-ML-310).
- Thread: slack #prompt-engineering: "separator vs tokenized slots" (2025-09).

End state goals for this doc:
- Converge on 2-3 recommended slot templates (separator and token-delim) with clear cache policies and trade-off table.
- Move final templates to shared prompt library with small integration tests.

Signed-off (scratch): Ava
